deviceReleases.title: Button Slots, Variations & Split View Support
notes: **Buttons, not just faders.** Any Knobbler slot can now be a Momentary or Toggle button instead of a continuous fader. In the app's Layout mode, pick a mapped slot and choose Momentary or Toggle; it jumps between two values you set, which default to the parameter's full range (min and max). Momentary holds the on value while pressed; Toggle flips between the two. Requires forthcoming Knobbler app version 2026.11.6 or newer.

**A rack's variations on a Knobbler page.** A slot can now hold an Instrument or Audio Effect rack's macro variations instead of a parameter, recalling them from the page like buttons. Map it from Bluhand: tap the Map button, tap the rack's variations, then tap a Knobbler slot. A variation shows an asterisk ("2*") once you've nudged a macro away from what it stored, and tapping it again restores it. Requires Knobbler app 2026.10.10 or newer.
**Support for Split view.** Forthcoming app version 2026.11.6 contains a new Split view, which lets you display any two app pages, one above the other.

**Scene launch and stop feedback.** On the Clips page, a scene button now blinks while its scene waits to start — the same quantized "launched, waiting for the bar" feedback a single clip already gave — and the Stop All button blinks while everything playing waits to stop. The same feedback appears in the forthcoming Split view, in Knobbler app 2026.11.6 or newer. Requires Knobbler app 2026.10.10 or newer.

**OSC API Updates** A user request to enable integrating other tools with Knobbler, this adds a `/mapN {path}` endpoint that allows parameters to be mapped to a Knobbler slot by the parameter's Live API path. Thanks Mike ([Dream Reactor](https://dreamreactor.net/))! See the [OSC-API](https://plugins.steinkamp.us/m4l-Knobbler4/OSC-API#tablet-to-knobbler4) doc for detail.

deviceReleases.title: Named Knobbler Pages
notes: **Named Knobbler pages.** Knobbler is no longer limited to two pages of 16. A Live set can now have up to 16 pages, each with its own name, and the app's new **Layout** mode lets you drag faders and XY pads to any spot on any page. Pages are added, renamed, reordered and deleted from the app. Requires forthcoming Knobbler app version 2026.10.9 or newer.

**One Knobbler tab on the device.** The device panel now has a single Knobbler tab with a page menu above the slots, kept in step with the app in both directions. The page shown can be automated: turn on Automate Page Chg and record the "Knobbler Page" parameter.

**Heads up for existing Page automation.** The Page tab's entries are now Knobbler, Bluhand, Clips, Mixer, Session. With "Knobbler 2" gone, existing automation of the Page parameter points one entry later than before (what selected Bluhand now selects Clips).

**Fixes and housekeeping.** Unmapping from the device panel now sticks instead of coming back on the next refresh. Knobbler's settings are now stored in one place within the set, and mappings in older sets carry over when they're opened. Mapped parameters follow track and device moves without the device checking every second, so large Knobbler setups cost less while nothing is changing.

deviceReleases.title: Master Cue Volume + Operator Bank Rework
notes: **Master cue volume.** The master track's cue (preview/headphone) volume can now be controlled from the app, and mapped to any Knobbler slot like other parameters. Requires forthcoming Knobbler app version 2026.10.7 or newer. Thanks Knobbler user Sam Beard for the request!

**Operator banks reworked.** The Oscillator A–D pages now control each oscillator's **waveform** in place of its level-from-velocity amount. Those velocity amounts moved to a new **Osc Extras** page, alongside each oscillator's phase.

deviceReleases.title: Edit Your Set From the Nav Panel
notes: New opt-in **Auto-Open Plug-in Windows** mode, from the app or the checkbox on the device's Bluhand page: as you move between devices, the plug-in editor window for the one you left closes and the new one's opens. Off by default. Needs Live **12.4.3** or newer — on older versions the control is disabled rather than quietly doing nothing.

The nav panel is no longer read-only. Long-press any row to **rename it, recolor it, reorder devices, or delete one** — tracks, devices and chains, without reaching for the computer. Live snaps colors to the nearest one in its own chooser, so you get the same color you'd have picked in Live. Requires the Knobbler app **2026.9.22** or later.
Deleting is deliberately narrow: devices and racks only, never a track or a chain, and never the Knobbler device your app is talking through.
**Fixes**

- Recoloring a track now updates its channel strip immediately, instead of holding the old color until you navigate away and back. - Jumping to, renaming or deleting a cue point no longer acts on the wrong cue after the cue list has changed.

**Under the hood**, another round of the memory work from v66. Reconnecting the app used to throw away and rebuild a whole channel strip's worth of Live watchers every time, and browsing devices on the Bluhand page leaked a little on every device and bank change. Both now reuse what they already have, so long sessions on large sets hold their performance better.

deviceReleases.title: Support for Pre-loading Clips and Mixer Tracks
notes: Scrolling the Mixer and Clips pages on a large set now shows **real values the moment a strip or clip slot comes into view**. Knobbler used to know only about what was on screen, so anything a scroll revealed sat empty or stale until the device caught up. The device now fills in everything off screen in the background, so the page is already populated when you get there. Requires the Knobbler app **2026.9.14** or later.
Faders and buttons on a strip you've just scrolled to now **control Live immediately**. Before, a touch that landed before the device had caught up with the scroll was quietly ignored.

Under the hood, the device still only *watches* what's on screen — watching every strip and clip slot would strain Live on a big set. It reads the rest at a gentle pace instead: short slices of work with pauses in between so Live stays responsive, a longer rest between full passes on bigger sets, and only what has actually changed gets sent to the app.
The device panel also reads "intentionally blank" on the Clips, Mixer and Session pages, which have no controls on the device itself.

deviceReleases.title: Blue Hand Follows Rack Chains
notes: The device page now follows Live's **blue hand**, so selecting a chain inside a rack switches the controls to that chain's device instead of staying on the rack. If you use racks to hold a chain per song, the surface now gives you that chain's macros as you switch.

Under the hood, Live keeps two separate "current device" pointers and they disagree inside racks: clicking a chain moves the blue hand into the chain, but leaves the track's *selected device* pointing at the rack. Knobbler was watching the latter, which is why the device page stuck on whichever device you clicked first.

Note: the blue hand only exists when a control surface is configured in Live's Preferences (Link/Tempo/MIDI). Without one, Live stops maintaining that pointer, so Knobbler falls back to the previous behavior of tracking the selected device.
Thanks to Jamie for reporting this.

deviceReleases.title: Recording Clip Feedback, Meters On by Default
notes: This release improves feedback while recording Session clips:

- A recording clip now reports a **growing length**, streamed live as bars.beats.16ths, so you can watch it grow as you record. - Clips that are armed-and-waiting now show a distinct **pending-record** state, so it's clear what's about to capture versus what's already rolling. Requires app version 2026.6.17 ore newer to make use of this. - Level **meters now default on** for new device instances.

As always, the app and device negotiate capabilities and use only the features they have in common, so you can mix and match versions freely — update one side, or roll back to reopen an older set, and it just works.

deviceReleases.title: Live Clip Progress, Mixer Meter Fix
notes: This release adds a live progress indicator to the Session clip grid. The phase pie and the pending-stop flash now stream in real time from the playing clip, so you can see exactly where each clip is in its loop right from your device. (Throttled and gated on transport playback to keep it light.)
Other fixes in this release:
- Mixer meters no longer print a warning on MIDI tracks. - Documentation: consolidated the USB / link-local connection guide.

As always, you can mix and match app and device versions freely — they negotiate capabilities and only use what they have in common, so updating one side or rolling back to reopen an older set just works.

deviceReleases.title: Massive Efficiency Gains, Theme Fixes, Track Rename Fix
notes: This release contains a massive amount of under-the-hood work on keeping the device footprint as small as possible in your Live Set. This has been a week of learning for me about how the Max symbol table operates, and how Max for Live interacts with it in good and bad ways. The result is a much leaner and faster Knobbler. I hope you can feel it too.
Additionally, this release contains fixes for non-dark themes. Rookie move. (shaking my head)
There's also a bugfix around track renaming or changing color. It's now tracked in real time in Knobbler as it should have been.

deviceReleases.title: Support multiplayer Knobbler; UTF-8 fix
notes: With app version 2026.5.25 or newer: Multiplayer Knobbler! Knobbler can now be disconnected from Live's "selected track" and "selected device" and navigate its own path — tap **Follow Sel** in the toolbar to unlock a surface, so multiple tablets can each drive their own track/device in one Live Set.
Also fixed a packet-encoding bug: things would break (blank nav/clips/mixer) if a track or clip name contained a non-ASCII (UTF-8) character.

deviceReleases.title: Back to Arrangement; multiplayer reliability
notes: Requires the latest app version to expose the new Back to Arrangement button.

**Back to Arrangement** — a new toolbar button mirrors Live's own. When Session clips override Arrangement playback, tap it to return playback to what's written in the Arrangement. It lights up orange whenever an override is active.

**Multiplayer reliability** — clip views now keep updating through long multiplayer sessions. Clip and mixer observers are bounded to a warm buffer around the viewport instead of growing without limit.

**Efficiency** — a new columnar OSC encoding (`col`) sends arrays of objects as named columns plus bare-value rows instead of repeating keys in every record, and any oversized payload is now chunked generically (`chunkAny`) — cutting bandwidth and packet overhead on busy clip grids and large sets.

deviceReleases.title: Arrangement Transport & Cue Points
notes: Arrangement transport control via the new `pos` capability: stream the song-position playhead (throttled ~20Hz) with song length and time signature, and scrub it from the app (`/scrub`). Stream the arrangement loop brace (`loop_start`/`loop_length`) with inbound `/loopStart` + `/loopLength` to set the loop edges. Add or remove a cue point at the playhead (`/addCuePoint`), rename one (`/renameCuePoint/`), and jump-and-delete (`/deleteCuePoint`). Reconnecting clients get cue points and position re-pushed.
Requires app version 2026.5.24 or newer.

deviceReleases.title: Support for Swap; Reliability Fix
notes: With app version 2026.5.22 or newer, swap or move a slot's mapping to another slot via the new `swap` capability. XY pairs survive a swap (only a move out of a pair splits it). Fix: detach Bluhand cue-point observers before dropping them.

deviceReleases.title: Massive performance update, works with 12.3 again
notes: Massive rearchitecture yielding big leaps in speed and efficiency. Works on Live 12.3 (and earlier) again.

Reworked the Max patch from a dozen [v8] nodes with a message-based routing infrastructure to a single [v8] with internal routing. Patcher simplified dramatically. Performance improved dramatically. Opportunities for efficiency abound.

Migrated from Live 12.4 / Max 9.1 specific [udpsend] usage (rawbytes) to conditionally use it if the Max is new enough. Otherwise falls back on using [udpsend] as usual. Also disables batching for older Max to avoid symbol table pollution problems that JSON payloads can create. See https://steinkamp.us/posts/2026-05-15-knobbler-and-the-max-symbol-table
Before:
After:

This version also introduces a new dict-based settings system that will bring new possibilities and reliability in the future. I plan to support legacy+new storage for 5 versions or a couple of months, then remove the legacy bridge settings code.

deviceReleases.title: WARNING: 12.4 ONLY Mixer mapping, migrate to [v8], implicit mute by solo
notes: UPDATE / NOTE: THIS RELEASE ONLY WORKS WITH Live 12.4 / Max 9.1 -- v61 restores compatability with 12.3 / 0.0
This release is a big one!

The big under the hood change is a migration from the legacy [js] (2011-era SpiderMonkey JS interpreter) to [v8] (modern, fast JS interpreter). This had a big cascading effect with huge positive performance impact for Knobbler. The biggest takeaway I cataloged here: https://steinkamp.us/posts/2026-05-15-knobbler-and-the-max-symbol-table

User-facing changes include support for the /mkMapN OSC messages, which the app uses to map Mixer elements to Knobbler sliders. In a future app release (>= 2026.5.19) there is a toolbar button to engage "Mapping" mode, where mixer elements indicate their ability to be mapped, tap one of them, then tap a Knobbler slider. The Main track Crossfader is supported too.
The mixer module also watches "mute_by_solo" on tracks so that their mute status can be propertly displayed when other tracks are soloed.

deviceReleases.title: P3SA Multi-Device Support, Optimize Performance
notes: This release enables Push 3 Standalone users to run multiple Knobblers instances and devices.
It does this by exposing the device listen port as a numeric parameter, so it can be changed on the P3SA.
It also includes a performance optimization where single-message OSC sends bypass the batcher.

deviceReleases.title: Performance for Physics
notes: This is a purely under-the-hood release with changes in Knobbler's core message sending and receiving architecture.

Forthcoming app changes will put different stresses on Knobbler, with the potential for many simultaneous continuous oscililations of parameter values from experimental physics-based models in Knobbler's controls. Fling an X-Y control around its original position and let it orbit forever.

deviceReleases.title: Honor "Select on Launch" Preference
notes: Honor Live's "Select on Launch" preference when firing clips and scenes from the Knobbler clip view -- previously these always selected the launched clip/scene regardless of the preference. Thanks to u/Jorne555 on Reddit for the report!

deviceReleases.title: Live 12.4 Readiness, P3SA
notes: This release focuses on readiness for Live 12.4.

In this upcoming version, many parameter names were renamed. Thanks so much to Knobbler user extrordinaire Niels Otto for alerting me to the problems in the 12.4 Beta. In doing this project, I simplified how the relationship between devices and parameter names is expressed. I moved it from a strange decompilation of the Push 2 control surface script and run through many text transformation filters to generate a valid Javascript file, then manual tweaks of course to make it work.
This new version is a YAML file that is read by a preprocessor who outputs Javascript with the same interface as the original monstrosity.

This version also adds a dozen devices to the list of custom device-banks in the YAML files. I hand-tuned them, but if you have ideas for better organization then please let me know or open a pull request on `src/deviceBanks.yaml`.
Thanks again Niels! 🫶

This update contains two .amxd files. - Knobbler4-v56.amxd -- The update you should use in your Live Sets. - Knobbler4-Push3Standalone-v56.amxd - An experimental version to be used with the Push 3 Standalone.
There is also a README.txt file with P3SA instructions and a plea :)

deviceReleases.title: Multi-device X-Y fix; Experimental performance boost
notes: Per-instance settings for multi-device support (X-Y pairs and meters state are now independent per device); Session page tab; Experimental performance improvement for mixer and clip view scrolling.

deviceReleases.title: Session view
notes: Provides support for verion 2026.3.31 of the app, which includes a new Session view. This version of the device contains changes to support that view, along with other performance enhancements designed to limit data floods when changing tracks rapidly.

deviceReleases.title: Clips View!
notes: Another big release for Knobbler this year -- Clips view! Requires app version 2026.3.24, whivh ias currently in beta, but update to be ready for it.

Full-screen multi-track mixer with per-strip observers and output meters; Clip view with grid state, scene management, clip launching/recording/deleting, and color editing; Current parameter display with lock/unlock; Sidebar mixer with real-time volume/pan strings; Auto-config for streamlined setup; OSC message batching for improved network performance; Solo count reporting; Live track color sync in nav and mixer; Fix LiveAPI .id string comparison bugs that caused console errors on track/device changes; Many stability and performance improvements.

deviceReleases.title: Mixer View; Data Bundling; Efficiency and Reliability
notes: This is a huge release! Inspired by the most popular end-user request, version 52 of the Knobbler4 device now has support for a Mixer View!
This functionality will be fully available once the new version of the app makes its way to the Apple App Store and Google Play Stores. I expect that to happen before Friday, March 6.
Support for real-time meters, even in multi-channel mixer view through the use of an efficient batching approach.
Intelligently allocates and re-uses resources in Ableton Live to scale to very large sets.
New communication architecture to chunk and batch OSC messages. Helps prevent against network floods and dropped messages.
A thorough reworking of how LiveAPI objects are allocated and re-used in the device. These changes have eliminated crashes and dramatically reduced CPU usage and "spinning beach ball" moments.

deviceReleases.title: X-Y Support; Large Set Reliability
notes: This is a significant release in that it contains support for X-Y controls in the forthcoming 2026.2.14 release of the app. In addition, large sets should work perfectly with Knobbler now. Large track and device inventory messages are now sent in smaller chunks and reassembled on the app side.
https://youtube.com/shorts/CtO5K97r9Wg

deviceReleases.title: Adds support for undo and redo toolbar buttons.
notes: Adds support for Undo/Redo buttons when used with version 2026.2.3 of the app or newer.

deviceReleases.title: Handle `/playCuePoint` message
notes: This update supports a forthcoming app update that adds a play button next to each cue point.

deviceReleases.title: Send Cue Point display time
notes: This release is a small change to add Bars.Beats.16ths display to cue points display. This requires the forthcoming Knobbler app version 2025.12.12.

deviceReleases.title: Cue Points Support
notes: This release adds the `/cuePoints [...]` OSC message to populate a list of cue points in the next app release.
It also handles the message `/gotoCuePoint N` which is what the app sends when a cue point is chosen.

deviceReleases.title: Support for Multi-Buttons
notes: This release adds the `/quantItemsN {list}` OSC message for a parameter. For quantized parameters, this message will contain a JSON-encoded list of value names for each quantized step.
This is used by a forthcoming version of the Knobbler app (2025.10.7) to display multiple buttons for parameters with between 3-8 quantized items.

deviceReleases.title: Support for button UI for toggles
notes: This release adds support for a forthcoming app release that supports toggle buttons in the UI instead of sliders for parameters with two possible states. This is done with the OSC message `/quantN X` where N is the slider slot number and X is the number of states, with 0 meaning continuous. If X==2, then the slider will be changed to a button.
Update now to be ready for the app update :)

deviceReleases.title: Fix missing VST param bug
notes: Thanks Peter Bäckgren for the bug report!

This release reverts a change in v42 that removed the last param from VST devices with the intent of fixing a CPU hog issue when changing presets with some plugins that do not emit parameter names/values in a friendly way.
There is still a bit of a CPU hit now, but it is better than before. Enjoy all of your VST parameters now!

deviceReleases.title: Observe track record arm status
notes: This release is a small bugfix. Somehow I had overlooked the need to observe the track's record arm status and report it to the mixer panel running in Knobbler. This change fixes that, so now toggling record arm status in the Live UI is properly reflected in the Knobbler UI.

deviceReleases.title: Fix VST Preset Bug
notes: Thanks u/Ahfekz on Reddit for alerting me to a bug where in most VST instrument plugins, changing presets would often bring the system to its knees if Knobbler was in the set. I have found the culprit -- when changing presets, VSTs will emit all parameters, and some will do so into the same parameter slot in Ableton. This was causing a flurry of activity being sent to the tablet, as the last slider on a Bluhand page was receiving every parameter value.

Some VSTs do this right (TAL J-8 is one that does) and most that I tried do it wrong (Moog Mariana, g-Force plugins, etc). The ones that do it right have a parameter slot per parameter, the ones that do it wrong just send every parameter into the same slot.

Anyhow, I did some defensive coding in Knobbler to protect agains these cases. There is still a bit of a CPU jolt when changing presets but it is far far less impactful than before, at least in my testing.

This release also lays the foundation for a better chain navigation UX that requires an app update to complete. Once that is out, when looking at a rack in the Navigation pane, you can tap on the chain item to show the list of chains again. Previously a tap on a chain item had no impact and thus navigating to chains was cumbersome.
No visual changes in this one.

deviceReleases.title: Optional Page Automation
notes: This relase makes automating page changes optional.

The page automation feature was originally added to make it possible to change Knobbler pages via automation in Arrangement view, but had the poor side effect of recording automation for all page changes while recording, which is not what most people want.
Thanks Jamie Lidell for the suggestion and feedback!

deviceReleases.title: /toggleGroup and Better Help
notes: This release adds support for receiving a new /toggleGroup {ID} OSC message. This message causes a given Group Track to be expanded or collapsed, depending on its current fold state.
It also improves the contextual help in Live, both in tooltips and in Help / Info text (mouse not shown hovering over Port box).
Also adds a "Quick Start" section to the help pop-up.

deviceReleases.title: Chain color for Bluhand and Current Param Slider
notes: This release improves the Bluhand and Current Param Slider experience by using the chain color if applicable.
Previously, those components would only use the containing track color. It is possible to set custom colors for rack chains, so those colors are now honored.

deviceReleases.title: Rework app discovery UX
notes: This release improves the app discovery and selection process to be more intuitive and reliable. Fixes a bug where discovery was not initiatied on device startup, causing unnecessary frustration for new users. Presents a prompt in the list to select a Knobbler App or to notify that no apps were found.

deviceReleases.title: Keepalive /ping /pong; Fix color issue
notes: This release supports a forthcoming app feature where a `/ping` message will be sent every 5 seconds. The device will answer that message with an immediate `/pong` response. This is intended to keep the network connection "warmed up" in the hopes that it prevents the situation where it seems Knobbler needs to "wake up" after a period of disuse. It seems this is a non-tunable behavior of iOS's network stack.

Also fixes a bug on the Bluhand page when switching devices that would send the old device color value to each slider immediately prior to sending the new device color value. This would sometimes result in sliders that were the wrong color.

deviceReleases.title: Audio Effect + Current Param Support (future app!)
notes: This release switches the Knobbler device to be an Audio Effect device. Several users have requested this in order to put Knobbler in the Main / Master track and not disrupt their existing templates or layouts. Made sense to me!

This release also adds support for Current Param functionality, which gives a persistent slider controlling the last selected parameter. This will be released in an app update soon, which will also support phones! So update now and be ready when that hits.

deviceReleases.title: Multiple Tablet / Instance Support
notes: This release adds a "Device Port" field, which unlocks the ability to run mutiple Knobbler devices, which unlocks the ability to use multiple tablets!
Instructions in the docs.

deviceReleases.title: Reliability Improvements
notes: This release removes support from the Clips functionality introduced in v33. It was a can of worms and I decided to shelve it for now.
Other changes in this release are just reliability improvements, mostly for if things get in an odd state.

deviceReleases.title: Support for variations, random macros, version checks
notes: This release adds support for rack macro variations., randomize macro values, and will now alert if a new device version is available.

Macro variation support is as much as I could get from the Live API, where Variation support is limited to only getting the number of variations. The currently selected variation index can be queried, but not observed. The variation names are not available.
Even with the limitiations, I think it's still a really great improvement.
Support on the iPad is currently in testing and will be rolled out ASAP!
Long-press a variation to delete it. Press the camera icon to capture a new variation. Press the dice icon to randomize all the macros.
Knobbler now checks if an update is available when it starts up. If one is available, the question mark icon will turn to a "!!".

deviceReleases.title: Resilience, Performance
notes: This release includes an important fix for some of Ableton's "forgotten" devices that do not have a standard JS API implementation, such as CC Control.
There is also a nice simplification of how the device name is built for the Bluhand page.
Fancy About page.

deviceReleases.title: Page Param, Auto-Collapse Racks
notes: This release connects the tabs in the device to the tabs on the tablet screen. This lets you trigger different Knobbler screens by automating or modulating the page tab parameter. Thanks @chapelierfou for the request!
It also contains support for new functionality in the iPad/Android app around toggling track children display, cleaning up racks when collapsing them, and other small improvements.

deviceReleases.title: Eliminate control surface requirement; More reliable nav
notes: This release eliminates the need to configure a control surface.

I had been relying on the "Blue Hand" icon (aka `live_set appointed_device`) which is only available when certain control surfaces are selected. I started using this long ago after trying and failing to use the `selected_device` property of the selected track. Well, either Ableton fixed this in Live 12 or I just got a little wiser and figured out that I could use `live_set view selected_track view selected_device`, which does not have the control surface requirement.

The release also makes the nav display more reliable in that it watches for color and name changes for the current track and updates the nav when that happens. It also will send the full nav payload on track changes, which in my testing did not slow things down to any perceptible degree. If you do observe a slowdown, please let me know.
Thanks to all who have written in with questions and suggestions so far!
Happy Knobblin :)

deviceReleases.title: Fix group tracks navigation bug
notes: Fix a bug where when looking at tracks inside of a group, the tracks would be shown at the end of the track list rather than where they should be in the hierarchy. Thanks again Andrew Carroll for reporting the bug.

deviceReleases.title: Fix Empty Track Bug
notes: This release fixes a bug in the track/device navigation where a track with no devices would cause some chaos.
Thanks Andrew Carroll for reporting the bug!

This is also the first `.amxd`-only release in quite a while. Knobbler for iPad is now generally available and I've moved on from TouchOSC. It's great software, but I wanted to go places that it couldn't. Long live TouchOSC!

deviceReleases.title: Fix VST Parameter Bug
notes: Fixes a bug that mostly shows up in configuring VST parameters, but was related to any time the set of parameters changes. Ended up simplifying some of how Bluhand works as a result. :) Thanks again Andrew Norris for the bug report!

deviceReleases.title: ACTUALLY fix parameter bug
notes: Thanks 1000x Andrew Norris for keeping me honest.
Check out Andrew's stuff: https://andrewnorris.uk/
Actually fixes the problem where adding parameters via "Configure" in VSTs would not properly update the Bluhand sliders in real time.
**** NOTE ** This is the final release that includes a supported TouchOSC .tosc template. Subsequent releases are only tested and supported with the native Knobbler app.**

deviceReleases.title: Watch track output status for mixer enable/disable
notes: Watch `has_audio_output` more closely to enable/disable mixer controls appropriately.
Thanks Andrew Norris for the bug report! Check out Andrew's stuff at https://andrewnorris.uk/
Still looking for beta testers for the Knobbler iPad app. Email me at zack@steinkamp.us if you are interested.

deviceReleases.title: Detect control surfaces; stability
notes: * Detect control surfaces and show a warning if not present (required for Bluhand) * Overhaul refresh system to be snappier and not get lost * Fix bug in exclusive arm code that would try to arm un-armable tracks and generate a warning in the Max console * Add `control_surfaces.txt` file listing control surfaces that will enable Bluhand functionality * Added `Debug` switch to toggle OSC logging to the Max Window * Publishes device version in OSC (`/deviceVersion Knobbler-v23`) so that the iPad app can validate it is new enough

deviceReleases.title: Exclusive Arm/Solo
notes: Add support to honor the user's exclusive arm/solo setting for the forthcoming iPad app.

deviceReleases.title: Handle collapsed groups; Stability
notes: This relase handles collapsed tracks and brings some additional stability and performance to Knobbler.
Native app is really shaping up. This could be it.

deviceReleases.title: Device on/off; Performance Improvements
notes: * Provides support for device on/off to the native app * Performance improvments (caching parent colors and parameter name => parm id list index)
Preview of unreleased iPad app:

deviceReleases.title: Support for better dropdowns; Automation state
notes: This is another release in support of the forthcoming native iPad app. The TouchOSC layout is unchanged from v9. Hopefully the iPad app can exit testing this week and go into the App Store :)

* Provides Track/Device data in a consistent format that has enough information so that the app can show a nice hierarchal display. * Shows automation state (red/grey circles) and parameter disabled state (green circle / grey slider).

deviceReleases.title: Session Record + Main Channel
notes: This small release adds Session Record (circle icon) functionality and adds the Main channel to the channel list.

deviceReleases.title: Track/device browsing, tempo controls
notes: More native iPad app functionality: * Browse all tracks and devices in your set in the Bluhand page * Tempo controls (metronome, tap tempo, tempo input box) * Rack macro parameters limited to visible number in Bluhand -- no more useless sliders

deviceReleases.title: Header Control Buttons Galore!
notes: Removed the title from the native iPad app and added a bunch of buttons.

This releaes supports the functionality and indicators in the row of buttons at the top. They are intended to mimic the buttons at the top of the Live window. I also added marker navigation buttons and brought back Toggle Record Enable.

deviceReleases.title: Knobbler bugfix for v13
notes: Fixes a critical bug with the v13 release. Again, I neglected to test the frozen version and ended up bundling an outdated bpatcher with the frozen archive. Max can be a PITA with stuff like this. Anyhow, sorry for the thrash.
v13 included some improvements for the forthcoming native iOS app, namely direct access to parameter banks and track/device nagivation controls.

deviceReleases.title: Tabbed Interface, Bluhand banks improvements, Bugfixes
notes: * New more compact tabbed UI * Bluhand device presets now in the UI * Fix bug with shortcut buttons that could make re-opening a set assign the buttons incorrectly * Curated parameter banks for some stock Live devices (not done) * Use `live.banks` for Max for Live devices on Bluhand * Fix small bug in Bluhand that was emitting errors into the console

deviceReleases.title: Bluhand+Knobbler bugfixes; Native app prep
notes: Thanks to Matthew Flook for reporting a bug in Bluhand that prevented initial values from being displayed. Also fixed a problem with Knobbler mapping. Both problems were related to Max's "Freeze" function pulling in files from other projects mistakenly and getting very old/odd versions bundled. I learned my lesson and will test more with the Frozen version, since now I know there can be real differences with un-frozen versions.
Also adds `/syn` message receiving, which responds with `/ack`. This will help the Native iOS/Android app (forthcoming) to provide positive confirmation that the connection is set up correctly.

deviceReleases.title: Bugfix for Current Param Knob crash
notes: Fixes a bug (#13) in the Current Param Knob functionality that caused a garbage string value to be displayed, and in some cases led to a crash.

The problem came from Current Param Knob errantly scaling the parameter value to a number outside of the parameter's min/max range, then passing that value to the parameter's `str_for_value` call, which appears to lack bounds checking for the value argument.
Thanks @[rds2024-3004](https://github.com/rds2024-3004) for the bug report!

deviceReleases.title: Simplifications, Bugfixes, Bundled .tosc Template
notes: This release includes some internal simplifications, important bugfixes, and a versioned/bundled .tosc file.

In reverse order, since there are essential changes to the `.tosc` file, I've versioned that and put it in the `frozen/` directory and put the versioned file in the .zip. Make sure that going forward the version of the .tosc template matches the version of Knobbler!

Bugfixes mostly are around displaying values of toggle buttons. The bug was that if a slider was controlling a toggle, the value would be displayed as "On" until the value reached zero. In reality, anything less than 1 will switch the toggle to "Off" state. The M4L routine that returns the string value of a parameter seems to have a rounding bug if you just ask it "What is the string value of 0.99?" it will respond with "On" even though the param itself would be showing "Off". Anyhow!

The other big change is under-the hood in how OSC messages are routed to different parts of this device (Knobbler, Bluhand, CurrParamKnob, etc). I replaced a tangle of `[regex ...]` objects with a JS file, simplifying things in the main patcher quite a bit and removing some error/bug potential from adding new messages.
Old:
New:

deviceReleases.title: Fix recall bug
notes: A wiley one, again partially due to moving to a single instance of the JS. Not complaining, except for the bugs that are hard to find.
If you mapped a parameter on Knobbler then made any change that would affect the order of the track or device (e.g. reordering devices or tracks) then the new path to the mapped param was not stored.
Also fixes some bugs around startup sequence.

deviceReleases.title: Use chain color / title if in a rack
notes: Previously, all parameters in a track would be displayed in Knobbler4 with the same color and track name.
This version changes that behavior so that if a parameter is in a rack (MIDI, Instrument, Audio Effect), then Knobbler4 will use the color and title of the Chain the parameter's device is in.
For those who use lots of racks, this may be a game changer.

deviceReleases.title: Fix #10 - Multiple sliders mapped to the same param don't update
notes: Thanks @rds2024-3004 for the bug report.
This release makes general fixes and improvements to how various locks are handled in the JS code.

deviceReleases.title: Telemetry
notes: This release adds a telemetry "ping" on load.

As an independent developer, it's beneficial to both me and the people who use my devices to know which devices are used the most. This change adds a small amount of telemetry to this device that runs when you add the device to your Live Set. It assembles a short string containing the device name, the hostname of the computer it is running on (not the IP), the type of OS (Mac or Windows), and the CPU type (e.g. "arm64"). This message is sent to a computer that I own and operate, who appends this message to a log file.
The device will function as normal if the telemetry fails for any reason. The telemetry does not block the loading or operation of the device.

deviceReleases.title: Device Presets in Bluhand
notes: Adds a row of buttons across the top of the Bluhand tab that you can assign to jump to specific devices. Tap to map, long-press (1.5 seconds) to unmap.
Video walkthrough of the new features! https://youtu.be/Y9Nx1VpCqVM

deviceReleases.title: Bugfixes, refinements
notes: Fine tuning of TouchOSC layout. Font size refinement, better alignment of header items.
Walkthrough video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1SvkGQ3_K8k

Bug Fixes: * Knobbler slider 25 was mislabeled 15 in the TouchOSC template. * In Bluhand, if a parameter value was purely numeric it would not show. * In Bluhand, if you were looking at bank > 1 and changed the device to a device with only one bank, the display would not be correct. Changed it so that it always starts at bank 1 when changing devices. * The Current Param Slider value was updating infrequently. Removed unnecessary slowdown code in its update routine.
Enhancements: * Added instructions for connecting between Mac and iPad via USB

deviceReleases.title: Bluhand + Double-tap default
notes: This release re-adds the Bluhand functionality from the prior major version of Knobbler. Bluhand lets you directly manipulate every parameter of the currently selected device on your iPad.
It's all implemented in pure Max and no Javascript (which was a source of slowness and crashes of Ableton Live in Knobbler3).
Also adds the ability to double-tap a slider to reset it to its default value.
Make sure you update the `.tosc` files on your iPad when downloading this release!

deviceReleases.title: Initial Release
notes: Introducing Knobbler4!
A ground-up rethink and rewrite of Knobbler3, bringing awesome performance and reliability, two things Knobbler3 started struggling with as it grew.
Knobbler4 is _noticeably_ less taxing on your computer, and so far (knock on wood) has been reliable for me.

Note that this release eliminates the Bluhand functionality from Knobbler3. That was the main culprit for the performance and reliability problems. I am looking into how I can fix that, since I came to really like it, especially combined with device shortcut keys.
Anyhow, give Knobbler4 a shot and let me know what you think. Thanks!
